drivingQuestion: Does a Torah scroll written in another language have sanctity?
outcomeNote: the contradiction is raised; its resolution falls outside this unit

segments.he: וּסְפָרִים נִכְתָּבִין בְּכׇל לָשׁוֹן וְכוּ׳. וּרְמִינְהוּ: מִקְרָא שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ תַּרְגּוּם, וְתַרְגּוּם שֶׁכְּתָבוֹ מִקְרָא, וּכְתָב עִבְרִי — אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם עַד שֶׁיִּכְתְּבֶנּוּ בִּכְתָב אַשּׁוּרִית, עַל הַסֵּפֶר, וּבִדְיוֹ.
segments.en: The mishna stated: Torah «scrolls are written in any language. And» the Gemara «raises a contradiction» from a baraita: A Torah scroll containing a Hebrew verse in the «Bible that one wrote in» Aramaic «translation,» or a verse written in Aramaic «translation that one wrote» in the Hebrew of the «Bible,» or that was written «in» the ancient «Hebrew script» and not in Ashurit, «renders the hands impure only if one writes it in Ashurit script, on a» parchment «scroll, and in ink.» Apparently, contrary to the mishna, a scroll written in a language other than Hebrew is not sacred.

moves.summary: baraita: only Ashurit renders the hands impure

edges.about: whether a scroll written in another language has sanctity: the mishna allows any language, the baraita requires Ashurit

positions.claim: scrolls may be written in any language
only Ashurit script on parchment in ink renders hands impure
